blocks.text: The Hebrew book is anonymous and takes its title, Eikhah, from its opening word, “How.” The chapter presents Jerusalem as a person: once populous and prominent, now portrayed as bereaved, abandoned, afflicted, and speaking in complaint. The shifts between description, Jerusalem’s own speech, and prayer to the LORD mean that the chapter should not be read as the straightforward autobiography of a single speaker.

Lamentations is a collection of five poems with distinct voices and formal patterns. Chapters 1–4 use alphabetic structures, while chapter 5 has twenty-two lines but does not continue the alphabetic progression. This places the first chapter within a larger, carefully shaped sequence of poems rather than treating it as an isolated lament.
